main_text.l: Ne timeas populè meus, habitans in Zion ab Assur: in virga percutiet te, & baculum suum levabit contra te in via Ægypti. Quoniam adhuc valde modicum, & consummabitur furor & indignatio mea in abolitione eorum. Et excitabit contra eum Dominus exercituum flagellum, iuxta cædem Midian in petra Oreb: & virga eius super mare, levabitq; eam in via Ægypti. Et erit in die illa, auferetur onus eius ab humero tuo, & iugum eius a cervice tua, & dissipabitur iugu a facie unctionis. Venit in Aiath, & transijt in Migron: in Michmas reponet arma sua. Transierūt vada, & in Gæba pernoctauerunt (veluti in) hospitio: territa est Rama:Gibea Saulis fugit. Hinni voce tua filia Gallim, fac audire Laisam, paupercu-lam Anathoth. Amota est Madmena:habitatores Gebim collegerunt se. Adhuc ipsa die stare poterit in Nob : agitabit manum suam versus montem filiæ Zion, collem Ierusalem. Ecce Dominus Deus exercituum deramificat frondem cum potentia, & (ligna) excelsæ staturæ succidentur, atq; sublimia humiliabūtur. Et resecabit condensa sylvæ per ferrum : atq; Libanus ipse per fortem(angelum)cadet.

page.notes: Doubtful: "populè" (final letter, read as è). A faint mark after "Ægypti." in line 9 may be a reference sign; not clear enough to transcribe. "iugu" in line 12 is printed as such and left unchanged. "dissipabitur" is printed with a long s that looks like f; read as dissipa-. The text is a continuous run of verses from Isaiah 10 and is copied as printed, not from the Vulgate.
